title: scale database capacity during a retail traffic peak
input: The retailer configures a supported Aurora engine, capacity range and application connection strategy.
action: Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts database capacity within configured limits while Aurora executes the SQL workload. The application manages transactions and connection reuse; capacity scaling is not request-level load balancing.
output: The checkout backend commits order rows and retrieves them without changing its SQL endpoint during normal scaling.
check: Exercise peak load, capacity ceilings and failover; verify engine-specific idle and scaling settings.

title: run an agent that retrieves authorized order status
input: The developer deploys an agent with explicit tool permissions and a bounded customer-support task.
action: AgentCore supplies configured agent infrastructure capabilities such as runtime, identity and tool connectivity. Agent code invokes the approved order-status tool with the permitted identity and enforces customer ownership.
output: The agent returns the retrieved order status with relevant evidence; write tools require their separate authorization policy.
check: Test cross-customer denial, tool authentication, timeout and untrusted tool-output handling before enabling the agent.

title: answer a policy question with retrieved document evidence
input: The user asks a policy question against an approved, indexed document collection.
action: Knowledge Bases retrieves relevant chunks from its configured source and vector store and can invoke a selected model for retrieval-augmented answers. Ingestion updates and document permissions determine the available evidence.
output: The application presents the answer and citations and sends unsupported questions to the policy owner.
check: Test stale documents, irrelevant retrieval and access boundaries; verify citations support each accepted answer.

title: orchestrate a document classification and extraction flow
input: The builder defines a versioned flow with permitted document input and branch conditions.
action: Bedrock Flows connects configured prompt, model and supported integration nodes, using defined inputs and conditions. Each node performs its own operation; flow wiring controls ordering and branch selection.
output: The document application invokes the published flow and stores only the validated classification and extracted fields.
check: Test every condition branch, missing fields and downstream failures using the published flow version.

title: release a tested customer-support prompt version
input: The prompt owner defines variables, model settings and representative support questions.
action: Prompt Management stores and versions reusable prompts with their supported model configuration. The release selects an accepted version; runtime model invocation happens through the application or its configured flow.
output: The application invokes the selected prompt version with validated variables and returns the model response for its support task.
check: Compare prompt versions against the evaluation set and verify rollback to the accepted version.

title: run a quantum experiment with reviewed classical preparation
input: The researcher prepares a supported circuit and selects simulator or available quantum-device execution.
action: Braket submits the quantum task to the chosen supported simulator or device and returns task results. Classical experiment code prepares inputs and interprets measurement statistics; device execution is not deterministic application inference.
output: The research notebook compares measured distributions across repeated runs and retains the experiment configuration.
check: Check device availability, circuit support, task status and statistical uncertainty before drawing conclusions.

title: join an authorized customer-support audio session
input: The customer application requests a support meeting after validating the case identity.
action: Chime SDK APIs create the meeting and attendee credentials for the application's communications session. Client SDKs exchange real-time media through the supported meeting infrastructure; the application controls participant assignment.
output: The authorized customer and agent communicate within the assigned session while the backend protects meeting credentials.
check: Test attendee authorization, reconnect behavior and meeting cleanup; prevent reuse of another customer's join credentials.

title: detect a broken checkout path before customers report it
input: The operator configures a scheduled canary using a restricted test account and nonproduction transaction identifiers.
action: CloudWatch Synthetics runs the configured API or browser checks and records execution results and artifacts. The canary exercises the selected checkout steps; it does not repair a failed application.
output: The on-call team examines the failed step and opens a checkout incident with the captured evidence.
check: Deliberately break a test endpoint, verify the alarm and ensure the canary cannot place uncontrolled real purchases.

title: review a code change for supported quality issues
input: The developer submits a repository revision with its supported language and review context.
action: CodeGuru's selected review or profiling capability analyzes supported code or runtime evidence. A code review produces recommendations; a profiling integration examines runtime behavior, so the owner chooses the relevant feature explicitly.
output: The developer validates relevant recommendations and updates the code through normal review.
check: Reproduce the issue and run regression tests; recommendations alone do not establish the application's correctness.

title: triage supported code-security findings before deployment
input: The security-enabled build supplies source artifacts within the approved scanning scope.
action: CodeGuru Security analyzes supported code to identify security findings and associated remediation guidance. The scan reports potential issues; it neither deploys the application nor automatically fixes every vulnerability.
output: The maintainer validates exploitability, repairs confirmed issues and decides release eligibility under the repository policy.
check: Run a follow-up scan and application tests against the repaired revision before accepting the finding resolution.
